A.explanation: At an antinode the two opposite waves do not stay in phase at $0^\circ$ at all times because both waves keep moving past the point.

B.explanation: A constant $180^\circ$ phase difference gives destructive superposition and zero resultant, which describes a node not an antinode.

C.explanation: An antinode is defined as the position in a stationary wave where constructive superposition gives the largest vibration amplitude.

D.explanation: Minimum, ideally zero, amplitude describes a node where the two waves cancel, not an antinode.

hints: Notice the stationary wave is formed by two identical progressive sound waves travelling in opposite directions.
Recall how the two waves add at a fixed point: in-phase addition makes a large resultant while antiphase addition makes cancellation.
Compare the definitions of node and antinode in terms of maximum versus minimum amplitude of the stationary wave envelope.
walkthrough: Identify the system: two progressive waves of same frequency and amplitude travel oppositely and superpose, so the resultant amplitude varies with position but does not travel.
State the rule: where the two waves repeatedly reinforce, the stationary wave has a vibration antinode with maximum amplitude; where they repeatedly cancel, it has a node with minimum amplitude.

Check the phase idea: because the component waves are moving, their instantaneous phase difference at a fixed antinode is not frozen at $0^\circ$ or $180^\circ$, so options about always $0^\circ$ or always $180^\circ$ do not define the antinode.
Conclude that the defining property is maximum amplitude of the stationary wave. This is option C.
